run.rulesInOwnWords: Six chambers in a line (1 first, 6 last). Whole non-negative masses; quarters and halves rounded down. All start LARVAL, masses 3,6,6,2,2,1, waste 0. Limit/pupation mark/return mark: 1=10/7/3, 2=8/6/2, 3=12/9/4, 4=6/5/2, 5=9/7/3, 6=7/5/2. Moult limit 38. Each cycle steps 1 to 5 in order, each finished for all chambers before the next. Step 1 feeding: add feed, limit ignored. Step 2 carry-forward: chambers 1 to 6 in order; excess above limit to next chamber, chamber set to limit; cascades; chamber 6 excess to waste. Step 3 stage check on post-step-2 masses: LARVAL at or above pupation mark becomes PUPAL; PUPAL at or below return mark becomes LARVAL; otherwise unchanged. Step 4: compute all six amounts from start-of-step masses and post-step-3 stages (LARVAL floor/4, PUPAL floor/2), apply at once; LARVAL amount to waste; PUPAL amount to chamber n-1, or waste for chamber 1; limit not enforced; cycle-5 excess never corrected. Step 5 moult if sum strictly greater than 38: halve all (floor), removed to waste, log cycle.
run.notes: Worked all five cycles by hand first, then wrote and ran a short Python script (rear.py) as an independent check; reproduced every quantity. Only metamorphosis.md was read. Cycle 5 total exactly 38, NOT more than 38, no moult. PUPAL chamber 1 discards its own half into waste in cycles 2 to 5. Chamber 2 ends at 10 over its limit of 8, left uncorrected since cycle 5 is last.
